First, we rewrite the integral as

$$
\int (x-100)^{7/4}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Now, we let  $u=x-100.$ Then differentiating with respect to $x$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We now write our integral in terms of $u,$ calculate the integral as normal, and write the final answer in terms of $u$ at the very end:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x-100)^{7/4}\,\text{d}x & =\int {u}^{7/4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{{u}^{11/4}}{11/4}+C \\  & =\frac{4}{11}(x-100)^{11/4}+C \\  & =\frac{4}{11}\sqrt[4]{(x-100)^{11}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's double-check that our result is correct. If we differentiate the result, then it should come out to the original integrand:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{4}{11}\sqrt[4]{(x-100)^{11}}+C] & =\frac{4}{11}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\sqrt[4]{(x-100)^{11}}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{4}{11}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[(x-100)^{11/4}]+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) \\  & =\frac{4}{11}\cdot \frac{11}{4}(x-100)^{7/4}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x-100)+0 \\  & =(x-100)^{7/4}\cdot 1 \\  & =\sqrt[4]{(x-100)^{7}}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
